title: DIVE: Scaling Diversity in Agentic Task Synthesis for Generalizable Tool Use
claim: Existing synthesis approaches limit diversity or verifiability and hurt generalization; evidence-first synthesis with real tools yields diverse, verifiable tasks.
layout: Stacked top-to-bottom: four prior-limitation panels with radar plot, then pink ours panel
description: A tall figure with a dark navy title banner, "Synthesize Diverse Agent Task for Generalization". The upper part is a white and blue panel listing four prior approaches in blue headers. These are fixed-toolset synthesis (DeepResearch + Search/Browse), extraction from specified pipelines, simulated tools, and query-first synthesis. Each approach is a small box-and-arrow diagram with a red label such as Low Diversity, Costly Scaling, Unverifiable Risk or Unsolvable Risk, plus a speech-bubble critique. At upper right is a radar chart over nine benchmarks. A gray base model is small, a blue fixed-toolset model is uneven, and a purple DIVE polygon encloses both. The lower pink panel presents DIVE. It has three stage labels (execute real-world tools, collect evidence, derive tasks). Under them is a graph of gray nodes that turn purple as evidence grows, next to a JSON tool-response snippet and a derived medical question and answer. The eye goes first to the red warning tags, then to the pink DIVE section.
caption: Motivation and overview of \method. Top: Fixed-toolset synthesis and pipeline pooling limit diversity and weaken generalization. Middle: Simulated tools and query-first synthesis for diverse tasks increase unverifiability/unsolvability risk, limiting agentic training. Bottom: \method performs evidence-first synthesis on diverse, real-world tools, producing verifiable and executable tasks. Radar: Gray: base model; Blue: trained on deep-research data synthesized with a fixed search/browse toolset (strong in-distribution but weak/negative transfer); Purple: trained on \method with matched data and training budget (robust generalization).
abstract: Recent work synthesizes agentic tasks for post-training tool-using LLMs, yet robust generalization under shifts in tasks and toolsets remains an open challenge. We trace this brittleness to insufficient diversity in synthesized tasks. Scaling diversity is difficult because training requires tasks to remain executable and verifiable, while generalization demands coverage of diverse tool types, toolset combinations, and heterogeneous tool-use patterns. We propose DIVE, an evidence-driven recipe that inverts synthesis order, executing diverse, real-world tools first and reverse-deriving tasks strictly entailed by the resulting traces, thereby providing grounding by construction. DIVE scales structural diversity along two controllable axes, tool-pool coverage and per-task toolset variety, and an Evidence Collection--Task Derivation loop further induces rich multi-step tool-use patterns across 373 tools in five domains. Training Qwen3-8B on DIVE data (48k SFT + 3.2k RL) improves by +22 average points across 9 OOD benchmarks and outperforms the strongest 8B baseline by +68. Remarkably, controlled scaling analysis reveals that diversity scaling consistently outperforms quantity scaling for OOD generalization, even with 4x less data.
